text:
sam (AE): heads up — large enterprise wants an on‑prem airgapped POC. asking: packaging constraints, upgrade cadence, and a pricing expectation they can sign to this month. can we sync?

maria (Solutions): +1. do we have a definitive packaging matrix for fully disconnected installs?

raj (SE): we have two flavours: full immutable bundle (tar.gz signed, sbom, kernel modules) and delta bundles for patching. delta requires an agent that can apply signed chunks.

ken (Eng): caveats: delta bundles reduce transfer size but add complexity for rollback and compatibility. sequence numbers and manifest verification mandatory. we can sign manifests with customer KMS if required. sample verify step:```bash
# on customer host
sha256sum rwd-bundle-v1.tar.gz
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json
```

eli (Customer): can we avoid an always‑on agent? security team prefers pull from secure USB or an internal repo, no outbound connections.

raj (SE): yes — we support agentless install via USB/airgap repo. for deltas, they'd upload signed delta chunks to the repo and the operator runs apply script. will require cust ops to run the apply; we can provide an approval script.

nina (Legal): legal/compliance asks: SBOM, vuln scan report, and list of third‑party licenses for the POC. also need to confirm no restricted crypto export concerns — please flag if FIPS/HSM is required.

ken (Eng): we can include SPDX SBOM and a weekly CVE snapshot for POC. for HSM/KMS integration: we support both customer HSM (PKCS11) and Redwood-managed signing for non-sensitive installs.

sam (AE): pricing — they asked whether offline/private is billed as reserved capacity or enterprise license. what are the options?

maria (Solutions): typical: 1) Reserved capacity (monthly commit) for Dedicated with private peering; 2) Enterprise perpetual + support + annual maintenance for on‑prem/airgapped. POC usually discounted (time‑limited).

eli (Customer): re: upgrades — do you recommend monthly small patches or quarterly full upgrades? ops wants minimal windows.

raj (SE): recommend monthly security deltas (small, signed) and quarterly feature rollups. bigger feature upgrades should be scheduled in maintenance windows; we can provide hotfixes out‑of‑band for critical issues.

ken (Eng): note: for customers who opt for agentless USB installs, monthly deltas need operator intervention. if they want automated patching, we need a controlled egress path or a pull proxy inside their network.

ops-bot: created ticket #SR-2026 for airgap POC packaging deliverables (owner: maria).

maria (Solutions): action list: 1) deliver immutable bundle + SPDX SBOM, 2) provide delta apply script and manifest verification docs, 3) draft POC SOW with cadence: monthly security deltas, quarterly upgrades, and a final acceptance test. i'll draft and loop legal.

nina (Legal): i'll review SOW and add export control clause and SBOM disclosure language.

sam (AE): customer asked about activation/entitlement keys and offline license checks — can we do time‑bound license files?

raj (SE): yes. we generate signed license tokens that validate locally (expiry/timebound). we can also support node counts in the token.

eli (Customer): ok — that sounds workable. we'll need estimated timelines and a cost ballpark for a 3‑month POC (1 node) and if we go to 10 nodes.

maria (Solutions): i'll produce POC quote: 3‑month POC (1 node): waived setup, discounted maintenance; 10 nodes: setup fee + annual maintenance. will send numbers by EOD.

sam (AE): perfect. can everyone review the draft SOW by tomorrow morning? cc @nina @raj @ken

maria (Solutions): will do. :thumbsup:

eli (Customer): thanks team — appreciate the quick turn.

sam (AE): closing loop — next sync after SOW + quote delivery.
